title: Rungs 3 and 4 of the bank ladder: κ = 7.11175695867958e-4, and the top of the complex ledger (priced target, not a witness)
body:
**A scheduled target, not a witness.** `kappa = 711599961413937/10^18 = 7.11599961413937e-4`
-- **+0.4671% over #224's rung 2** and **+4.1584% over the #207 frontier** -- conditional on
the same open obligations rung 2 carries, plus two new inventories. The bank schedule those
rungs need is **built here, not merely owed**: every bank exactly filled, every item in a block,
the remainder padded from a retained bin.

Package: `research/complex-bank-run3/`, self-contained on `main`: it vendors #219's rung-1
package byte-identically under `references/pr219-run1/` and #207's frontier certificate, and
pins 27 files by sha256.

```sh
cd research/complex-bank-run3 && python3 -B verify.py
```

## The ladder, and where it stops

Rung 2 (#224) absorbs the complex word's rank-11 family and lands on the complex branch's
ceiling, so every further rung has to raise the **complex** coarse saving. The criterion that
makes such an absorption free is that the family's own volume is a whole number of width-66
banks (`66 | rank * children`), and exactly three families of that ledger satisfy it:

| rung | what leaves the ledger | per bank | banks | complex coarse | kappa | vs rung 2 |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 2 (#224) | complex rank 11 | 6 rank-11 blocks | 531 | 7.08793603125109e-4 | 0.000708291570590726 | — |
| 3, volume criterion | + complex rank 16 | — | 192 | 7.11077971348264e-4 | 0.000710572698755137 | +0.3221% |
| **3, padded schedule** | + complex rank 16 | 4 blocks + 2 registers | **198** | **7.11289982558164e-4** | **0.000710784408728476** | **+0.3520%** |
| 4, volume criterion | + complex rank 20 | — | 60 | 7.11681826686289e-4 | 0.000711175695867958 | +0.4072% |
| **4, padded schedule (the top)** | + complex rank 20 | 3 blocks + 6 registers | **66** | **7.12106696511698e-4** | **0.000711599961413937** | **+0.4671%** |

The two "volume criterion" rows are the accounting the criterion gives and are kept because
they are what the ledger arithmetic produces -- but a width-66 bank cannot host them (`192` and
`60` are below the capacity bounds `198` and `66`, and no uniform tiling absorbs two bins at
once). The padded rows are the schedule a bank admits, and they price higher, so the padded
rung 4 is the top this PR claims.

After rung 4 **no family of the remaining 17 has a whole-bank volume** (the check is
machine-asserted), so the accounting criterion the built rungs use is exhausted: 795 banks in
total (531 + 198 + 66), top row `W = 35,361`, rank mass 2,329,866, 634,473 children, largest
child 19. Each step keeps the row identity `66 * W - rank_mass = 3,960` and drops the stock by
exactly the bank count (531, 198, 66).

Two consequences fall out of the same arithmetic, and they are the useful part:

* reaching `kappa = 7.2e-4` needs a complex coarse saving of `7.20518773516934e-4`, i.e.
  **+1.1809%** more than the top rung's -- more banking than the remaining mass can supply at
  this width;
* while the complex branch caps the budget, the assembly's ceiling is capped by #219's rung-1
  bit leaf, so **`kappa = 7.5e-4`, `8e-4` and `1e-3` are unreachable on this bit word**, whatever
  the complex ledger does. Those targets need a new bit supplier first.

## Status (unchanged blocker, two new items)

`obligations.json` states C1-C7 and inherits #219's R1-R4; T1, which this PR carried as an
obligation, is settled below. Read from the pins rather
than asserted: the complex supplier's certificate carries **no key containing `bank` at all**,
and the only banked word in the pins is the **bit** word's entrance-gauge pack (#205, 45,842
banks of width 72 over rank-60 exteriors). Nothing enumerates the complex word's rank-11,
rank-16 or rank-20 children, so the item-to-block map has no starting inventory (C6, C7). And
because `66 = 4 * 16 + 2 = 3 * 20 + 6`, the two new families cannot tile a bank alone.

**T1 is now enumerated, and the answer is negative** (`schedule66.py`, `schedule66.json`,
re-run by `verify.py`). A uniform pattern -- the same pattern in every bank, as the certified
bit-side construction uses -- forces one common bank count `B` with `k_f = n_f / B`, so `B`
divides `gcd(n_f)` and `sum_f k_f * f <= 66`. That is exhaustive:

| family | blocks per bank | banks by volume criterion | banks its capacity needs | uniform patterns |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| 11 (rung 2) | 6 (`66 = 6 * 11`) | 531 | 531 | 4, tightest **531** |
| 16 (rung 3) | 4 (`66 = 4 * 16 + 2`) | 192 | **198** | 4, smallest **198** |
| 20 (rung 4) | 3 (`66 = 3 * 20 + 6`) | 60 | **66** | 3, smallest **66** |

No subset of two or three families admits a uniform tiling at all; `{16, 20}` comes closest,
its common divisor 198 giving four rank-16 and one rank-20 block per bank -- 84 registers into
a 66-wide bank. The volume criterion and the capacity criterion coincide only when the rank
divides the width, which is why rung 2's `531` is consistent and the unpadded `192` and `60`
are not.

**T1 is settled, at the schedule level** (`prototype66.py`, checked by `verify.py`, recorded in
`certificate.json` -> `padded_schedule`). A bank the family cannot fill alone is filled by the
family plus a fixed pattern of retained blocks:

| rung | banks | per bank | padding per bank | chosen draw |
| ---: | ---: | --- | ---: | --- |
| 11 | 531 | 6 rank-11 blocks | 0 | none |
| 16 | 198 | 4 rank-16 blocks | 2 | 2 rank-1 blocks per bank (396 rank-1 children of 262,602) |
| 20 | 66 | 3 rank-20 blocks | 6 | 6 rank-1 blocks per bank (396 rank-1 children) |

Every bank is exactly full, every family item lands in a block with no slot unused
(`4 * 198 = 792`, `3 * 66 = 198`, `6 * 531 = 3,186`), the item-to-block map is explicit (item
`i` -> bank `i // k_f`, block `i % k_f`), and the padding is a partial draw from a bin the
ledger keeps, so the retained histogram carries the reduced count. Because the mass leaving is
`banks * 66` by construction, the row identity holds and the stock falls by exactly the bank
count at every step. All padding options are enumerated and compared (rank 16: two; rank 20:
eleven), and the best is the one claimed. What this is not: the normalizer, frames, charts and
prime witnesses remain C1-C7, and the padding blocks are ordinary retained children -- no new
frame family is introduced.

## Is the bank width a lever? No -- and the scan says which lever *is* one

The bank width is not a schedule parameter, it is the word's own modulus. The pinned
bit-side schedule fixes it: `M = 72`, its rank-22 bin's 20,016 occurrences carrying
`22 * 20,016 = 440,352` registers into `440,352 / 72 = 6,116` banks, with the stock dropping
by exactly the bank count. So a width scan is a word scan (`widths66.py`), and it answers:

* **nothing narrower exists.** The engine's contraction is `rank mass < W * modulus`, and the
  pinned row has `rank mass / W = 65.8905...`, so every `w <= 65` leaves the row unposeable
  (recorded at 48, 54, 58, 60, 63, 64, 65). 66 is the smallest modulus this ledger admits.
* **nothing wider is comparable.** Holding the ledger fixed while raising `w` leaves a row whose
  rank mass fills only `mass / (W * w)` of its capacity: 99.834% at 66, **95.5% at 69, 91.5% at
  72, 68.6% at 96** -- a different word, which is why only the pinned width is priced, and where
  the scan reproduces this PR's own top exactly as its calibration.
* **the criterion is not the cap, the density is.** At `w = 54`, nine of the 20 families would
  tile whole banks and **1,549,098 registers (65% of the rank mass)** could leave, against
  52,470 (2.2%) here. A *less* dense complex word -- more stock per unit of rank mass -- would
  admit a narrower modulus where far more of its ledger tiles at once. That is what to look for
  in a new supplier, measured rather than guessed.

## What is instanced, and what is still owed

The schedule's items are now addressed (`instantiate66.py` -> `occurrences66.json`), which is
C1's combinatorial half and the C5-C7 inventories: item `i` -> bank `i // k_f`, block
`i % k_f`, offset `(i % k_f) * rank`.

| family | per vertex | items (3 copies) | banks | blocks per bank | padding registers | table digest |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| 11 | 1,062 | 3,186 | 531 | 6 | 0 | `fb9bd2d17f69...` |
| 16 | 264 | 792 | 198 | 4 | 396 | `f96efd45d9d9...` |
| 20 | 66 | 198 | 66 | 3 | 396 | `f9d9567b4b41...` |

**4,176 items over 795 banks**, 792 registers of padding (0.30% of the kept rank-1 bin), every
bank exactly filled, every block exactly one item, a per-family digest over the whole table, and
the ledger re-derived with the stock falling by exactly the bank count. What stays owed is read
from the pins rather than asserted: the complex supplier's certificate has **no key containing
`bank`** and its own status line says a literal globally renumbered operation program **is not
exported**, so the residual projectors the normalizer must move (C1's physical half) are not
there, and C2-C4 plus each child's frame/chain identity (C5-C7) follow the same gap. The *shape*
owed is pinned for the bit word at `references/pr219-run1/inputs/absorbed-occurrences.json`.

## Verification

* `verify.py` (exit 0) pins 27 files by sha256, rebuilds the whole complex-side ladder from
  pinned bytes, recomputes both paid moments per rung on the `10^-18` grid, runs the two
  unchanged 47-constraint assemblies with the adjacent grid points rejected, and reproduces
  #207's, #219's and #224's published grid points **exactly** (`a_complex` and both kappas
  asserted equal, not within a tolerance). The independent replica at my #208 pricing model's
  convention reproduces #208's own published rung-2 value `3541457/5*10^9`.
* A separate re-derivation written against the raw pinned bytes with plain integer and
  `Fraction` arithmetic -- no package module and no engine -- re-checks the row identities, the
  three volumes, stock-drop-equals-bank-count, the eligibility list `{11,16,20}`, the
  exhaustion, both kappa values, both ceiling landings, the gains and the next-step targets.
* The T1 scan is re-derived independently here, by brute force over every bank count instead
  of by the package's divisor logic: same pattern sets, same capacities, same obstruction. The
  padded schedule is re-checked as well: banks, blocks per bank, saturation, the padding draw,
  the stock drops 531/198/66, the padded top above the volume-criterion rows, and the
  exhaustion of the criterion afterwards.
* The width scan is re-derived as well: which widths are poseable, that only the pinned one is
  priced, and that the scan reproduces this PR's top at 66; and the instanced schedules are
  re-checked (795 banks, 4,176 items, 792 registers of padding, saturation, exactly-filled
  banks, the digests, the stock drops 531/198/66).
* Line endings are LF throughout (`schedule66.py`, `widths66.py`, `instantiate66.py`, the
  regenerated JSON, all sources) and every pin matches the stored bytes, so the checks pass on a
  fresh clone (verified in a clean worktree of this commit).
* Not run: upstream CI, and any contributor verifier other than the vendored #219 package
  invoked in place.

## Scope and limits

* **Not a witness**: the accounting, the padded bank schedule and the item addresses are
  certified; C1's physical half, C2-C4 and the inherited R1-R4 are open, so no normalizer, chart
  or physical witness is built. Not an unconditional multiplication theorem, not a practical
  multiplier, not a Lean certificate.
* T1 is settled (enumeration plus the padded schedule), and what it settles is a *schedule*:
  the bank geometry, the item-to-block map and the padding draw are checked, the normalizer,
  frames, charts and prime witnesses are C1-C7.
* The whole-bank volume condition is necessary and is what the built rungs use; it is not
  sufficient -- for the two new families it is not even compatible with a width-66 tiling at
  the bank count it prices, which is why the padded schedule exists.
* Nothing here bounds any other complex-side lever: this ladder is over this supplier's child
  ledger at this bank width. A different word, width or frame layout is not priced.
* The `10^-10` supplier field is priced too (`certificate.json` -> `conservative_variant`)
  rather than ignored.

Credits: rung 1, its schedule, the interval-moment engine and the 47-constraint assembly are
**#219** (vendored, imported, not re-implemented); the frontier and the complex ledger's shape
are **#207**; rung 2 and the ceiling argument are **#224**; the ladder and the `10^-10` replica
convention are **#208**; the bank proof and engine chain are #200/#205 (Chafik Boukhalfa and
the #197/#205 line) and #184/#168-v4 (icekylinx, eumemic) as inherited through them. This
package adds the rank-16 and rank-20 absorptions and their prices, the exhaustion proof and
the next-step arithmetic. Apache-2.0; no existing file is changed.
